constraints.evidence: Slide 13/8: A peak -$2.4M (stress $3.9M, 22% of cap) vs $18M cap; B reaches -$20.8M, 115.5% of cap. B at the 2.6 median ($25.5M) is not computed, but the cap test is built into the headline.
Slide 17: A cumulative cash end-2030 is +$2.40M at 25%, +$0.38M at 28%, -$2.32M at 32%. Break-even ad cost 28.6%. B never pays back; J +$1.8M.
Slides 13/22/23: A lowest group margin 9.3% (9.1% at 32%), B 4.5% in 2027, J 10.1%. Checked year by year; 2027 identified as the lowest year.
Slides 13, 14, 20: Option J is costed and compared (1.8x operating profit by 2030). Document states 'management can run one major launch at a time' and uses Japan as the fallback slot.

Slide 15: A reaches $26.4M, not $40M. Even B's $37.6M misses. The ambition is read as a path, with 2031-32 projected at $34.2M and $44.2M as an upper bound. Both the dating and the 1,667k-unit gap are given.
Slide 9: 4.0 removal line against a 2.6 median at 4% awareness. Slide 19 gate 5: raises the CEO's 15% trigger to 20% because the 10-20% band median is 3.5, below 4.0; 20% is 'needed, not sufficient'.

Slide 12: $24 price, 3.6 referral, 5.1 FBA, 3.5 product, 1.075 freight and duty, 6.72 ads, $4.005 contribution; $10.73 before ads. Retail at $7.55 a unit on slide 8. Payback built on contribution, not revenue.
Slide 17/22: $9.2M fixed and setup cost over 2027-30 against $11.3M contribution. B fixed cost $9.6M a year plus $1.3M setup and launch fee and $1,100 per door fixtures (slide 23).
Slide 17/18: $1.68M year-end inventory is deducted. Slide 22 shows the inventory build by year; four months of landed cost is a stated team-model assumption.

Slides 13/17/18: 28% pilot as base, 32% benchmark median (range 26-38%) shown as a separate case (-$2.3M), break-even 28.6%. The 25% plan figure is shown only as a reference case. The headline still treats 28% as the recommended case.
Slide 17: 25% duty alone gives -$0.74M at 28%; stress case -$3.4M. Slide 19 gate 2: on a mid-2027 rise, tighten the ad ceiling to 26.9% and re-run the plan.

Slide 6: Korean-only label complaint (6%) is 'fixed by the US labels in setup'. Slides 20 and 24: MoCRA registration, entity and English labels in Q1-Q2 2027. Setup $0.8M and $0.5M a year are in the fixed costs.

Slide 6 gives 29% vs 31% vs 48%. Gate 4 sets a repeat trigger at 31%. But the headline volumes remain the planning team's 300k to 1,100k ramp, and the document does not show how the ramp depends on repeat or the added SKUs.

alternatives.evidence: Slides 8, 9, 10, 23: Option B is run on the board's tests, fails the cap, payback and margin floor on its own 4.5 units/door. Its 4.5 is shown to match survivors, the 1.3x halo is rejected because the 0.71 correlation cannot show causation, and Mooncrest is cited.

Slide 20 has 'Specialty retail: Test doors only if gate 5 is met' (retail no earlier than 2029). No limited-door pilot in 2027 is costed, no scaled marketing or field cost is stated, and no comparison is made against Option A's thin payback.

Slides 13 and 14: Option J is costed (peak -$1.1M, +$1.8M by 2030, margin 10.1%) and compared year by year with A. The document says why A is preferred (1.8x by 2030, bigger prize) and keeps J as the fallback slot. No explicit trigger for a deferred US launch.
No variant with a smaller US team or lower off-Amazon brand spend. Fixed cost of $2.1M a year is taken as given, and no fixed-cost cut is tied to the break-even ad cost.

sensitivities.evidence: Slide 17-19: cumulative cash at 25% +2.40, 28% +0.38, 28% with 25% duty -0.74, 32% -2.32, 32% with duty -3.43. Break-even ad cost 28.6%, falling to 26.9% on a duty rise. Stress peak $3.9M. Gate 1 states the response.

Slide 9: 2.6 / 3.5 / 4.6 medians by awareness band against the 4.0 line, and a 20% awareness requirement. Slide 8: B needs about 32 units/door/week to cover fixed cost. The B peak at 2.6 units/door ($25.5M) and the effect of removing the 1.3x halo are not computed.

Slide 18: 4% fewer units miss payback at 28%. Gate 3 triggers below 96% of plan (288k units in 2027). Slides 10 and 19 name Saebom against Gaon Lab and Yeoreum and set a repeat gate. Not shown: the 20% cushion at 25% ACoS, or the 1.8x step up from the pilot run-rate.

overclaim.quote: Passes all three tests if ad cost is held near the pilot's rate (slide 13) / Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon … and cap ad cost below about 29% of sales, the line for payback by 2030

omissions: The 28.6% ad-cost ceiling is treated as controllable ('cap bids'), but the document does not show what capping bids does to volume. Gates 1 and 3 can pull against each other, and the plan's volumes already have only a 4% cushion at 28%. The agency benchmark says click costs rise with scale.

The slide 18 caveat that a 4% Amazon returns allowance cuts the break-even line to 24.6%, below the pilot's 28%, is not carried into the headline numbers or the 'passes all three tests' claim. If any return cost applies, the recommended base case misses payback.
The 2027 volume of 300k units is about 1.8x the pilot's June run-rate (168k a year on three SKUs). The document does not say how much of the step depends on the four added SKUs or on repeat.
No leaner fixed-cost variant of Option A, and no costed limited-door retail pilot, is offered as a cheaper way to protect the thin payback margin or to test the 4.0 units/door line before 2029.

The document does not recommend a response if the tariff rises beyond 'tighten gate 1 to 26.9% and re-run'. At 28% ACoS with 25% duty the case already fails payback, and the document does not say whether the launch should be reduced or stopped, or by when.
unsupported_assumptions: "if gates fail at end-2027, switch to Japan in 2028": assumes the Japan scale-up delivers Table 7 economics when started a year late. The pack models it only for 2027.
"Waiting a year: US revenue in 2030 would sit near $20.4M": assumes a delayed launch simply follows year 3 of the current ramp. No basis is given.
"Cap bids to hold the ceiling even if volume slows": assumes Amazon ad cost can be held at or below 28.6% at scale, against the 32% agency median for brands growing from $5M to $20M.
Planning-team Amazon volumes (300k to 1,100k, with four added SKUs at hero-product economics) are adopted as the base case with no build from pilot and repeat data.
"Doors followed Amazon scale" (slide 10): inferred from Saebom alone to counter the board memo's 0.71 correlation.
Japan comparison (1.8x, $1.8M cumulative): operating profit stands in for cash, so it is not a like-for-like payback comparison.
